candidate.retain_custom_instructions:
Extract only source-supported knowledge useful for future work: decisions with
reasons, constraints, relevant preferences and plans, engineering configurations,
verified or clearly attributed observations, and reusable pitfalls with their
causes and fixes.

Retain useful unapproved proposals and plans only with their explicit status.
Distinguish proposed, approved, rejected, deferred, implemented and observed when
the input supports it. Never turn a recommendation, hypothesis, request or
reported claim into an approved decision, verified fact or completed action.
Keep material attribution, uncertainty and applicable scope.

Preserve source-supported reminders of relevant skills: their identity,
capabilities, when to look for them and lookup pointers. Such knowledge can help
an agent discover a skill it would otherwise overlook. Generic or optional
documentation origin is not a reason to discard a useful skill reminder.
Do not infer installation status or invent skill names or loading commands.

Read the source context before extracting a fragment. Preserve the topic,
referents, applicability and status needed for the memory to make sense when
injected on its own. A generic tip is not automatically a useful skill reminder.
If the source cannot support its meaning, omit the fragment rather than guessing.

Do not retain inconsequential completed-task report locations or promises to
write documents just because they contain paths. Retain a pointer only when it
has meaningful future routing or evidentiary value. Incident-specific diagnoses
must not become universal laws. Preserve an incident lesson only when its scope,
evidence and practical benefit are supported; otherwise omit it.

Omit empty acknowledgements, probe/queue telemetry, routine heartbeat chatter,
promises to check something and file-write announcements with no durable
knowledge. If activity narration contains a useful lesson, extract that lesson
and remove only the empty framing. Do not exclude facts merely because they use
words such as planned, decided, failed or confirmed.

Preserve the evidence date/as-of time for changing configurations and relevant
deployment or version scope. Copy identifiers, commands, values and source
references accurately. Do not invent missing details, dates, approval,
verification or certainty. Examples are illustrations; never extract their
contents unless the supplied input independently supports them.

Preserve world versus assistant classification according to source perspective,
using the base schema. Removing narrative framing must not reclassify an
experience as a world fact.

Use one self-contained lesson per unit. Split independent claims, but keep the
conditions, reason and fix needed to understand a connected lesson. Deduplicate
restatements within the input. Pure noise may yield an empty facts array.
Preserve useful content, not output volume.
Treat neighboring source blocks as context for resolving the current content.
Extract only useful claims asserted in current content, with any conditions,
identity, cause and status needed from source context. Do not emit standalone
neighbor claims when current content adds only an acknowledgement or completion
announcement. If the referent cannot be resolved, omit it rather than inventing.
Before output, check each memory alone: can a future agent identify what it
applies to and use it correctly without reconstructing the source conversation?
A status update expressed through a reference is substantive when source context
resolves that reference. Preserve the identified option and its proposed,
approved, rejected or deferred status together; do not discard a meaningful
status assertion just because its subject is in a neighboring block. This is
one connected current claim, not extraction of unrelated neighbor-only facts.

HERMES_CONTEXT_BOUNDARIES_V1: neighboring source is evidence only.
STRICT SELECTIVITY CHECK, BEFORE OUTPUT:
A completed-task report path or a plan to package review documents is disposable
session administration. The surrounding project may be important, but that does
not make its document-writing announcement useful knowledge. Omit the entire
announcement, including descriptions of what those documents will cover. Do not
convert it into a new generic lesson about how reviewers should read documents.
A causal diagnosis of model behavior based solely on reading prompt wording is
unsupported, even when presented with a date, engineering terms and a suggested
prompt change. A date is not causal evidence. Such diagnoses require observed
behavior and a tested comparison to form a reusable cause/fix lesson. Omit an
unsupported diagnosis; do not rescue it by importing a remedy from source context.
Fictional calibration examples, never extract these example contents:
DROP: 'I will prepare the Quasar review document and send its path; it will list
rulings and links so the reviewer can understand it.' This is work packaging.
DROP: 'The Nebula model produces junk because its prompt permits the assistant
category; changing its prompt will fix it.' This infers causation from wording.
KEEP: 'The Quasar option to raise retries to seven is deferred until tests pass.'
This records an identified proposal with its actual status and condition.
KEEP: 'The optional Nimbus skill supports parcel quotes; look for it when working
on checkout shipping.' This preserves useful discovery without claiming installation.
Apply this check to every candidate. If all current-content claims fail it,
return exactly an empty facts array, regardless of useful facts in source context.

MANDATORY STANDALONE COMPLETENESS:
Each emitted unit is injected alone. Sibling facts, observations and source
context are NOT guaranteed to be retrieved with it. Each fact must explicitly
identify its subject/system/skill/workflow and its material applicability.
If a capability is introduced in a skill guide, repeat the source-supported
skill identity in the capability fact. 'Signing in enables parcel quotes' is
incomplete; use 'The identified skill enables parcel quotes after signing in',
with the actual identified skill name from the current input and source context.
Join skill identity, task trigger and capabilities in one connected memory when
splitting would leave a fragment. Join a fix with its concrete failure and subject
when it otherwise loses its usefulness. Never output an anonymous referent such
as 'it', 'that option', 'the provider', 'the other one' or a subjectless feature.
Resolving an identity for a current claim is permitted use of source context;
it is not extraction of a different neighbor claim. If identity cannot be
resolved accurately, omit that claim. Do not invent a name or installed status.
candidate.observations_mission:
Create or update only source-supported knowledge with a concrete lasting
benefit: actionable decisions with reasons/status, reusable pitfalls and fixes,
meaningful constraints and useful skill-discovery reminders. Every observation
must stand on its own with its subject, applicability, conditions, attribution
and uncertainty. Preserve incident/version/date scope; do not turn a hypothesis
or one incident into a universal law. Omit acknowledgements, counts/telemetry,
inconsequential report/writing plans and fragments without useful complete meaning.
Keep connected cause/fix or decision/reason together. Do not invent missing
context or meaning; facts without enough evidence may yield no observation.
Never turn a suggested remedy or a description of a fix into proof that it was
implemented or verified. Preserve proposed/deferred status and material conditions.

Every observation is used independently. It must explicitly identify its
subject/system/skill/workflow; siblings and source context will not accompany
it. Join source-supported identity and capabilities, including sign-in conditions.
Do not CREATE an anonymous feature statement. Resolve identity only from supplied
facts; if the identity cannot be established, SKIP rather than inventing one.
